pictures.t: Structural evolution of the Fucino basin
pictures.c: Structural evolution of the Fucino Basin according to Galadini (1999). The first half-graben was created by the activity of Tre Monti Fault starting in the Pliocene; the NW-trending faults along the eastern side of the basin became the most active only during the Quaternary (from Galadini [1999]).
Geological and geomorphological map of the Fucino Plain and location of surface ruptures produced by the 1915 earthquake (from Michetti et al. [1996]).

pictures.t: Summary of paleoearthquakes in Fucino region
pictures.c: Summary of earthquake occurrences in the Fucino Plain. High reliability is given to events that were identified on different strands of the main fault (red dotted lines). The age intervals depend on the data available (from Galadini et al. [1997]).

Tectonic/kinematic model of regional extension according to Piccardi et al. (1999). The left-lateral shear zone induces CCW rotation of blocks bound by NW-striking faults east of the Fucino; the latter exhibit right-lateral oblique slip (from Piccardi et al. [1999]).

pictures.t: Profile of Roman channel in former Fucino lake
pictures.c: Topographic profile showing the trend of a Roman channel displaced along the Trasacco branch of the main Fucino fault (from Galadini et al. [1996]).

pictures.t: Structural map of the Fucino basin and surroundings
pictures.c: Seismotectonic map showing the trace of the Ovindoli-Pezza fault system, major active faults of the area and distribution of recent seismicity. The surface breaks of the 1915 earthquake are highlighted by dots (from Piccardi et al. [1999]).
Geological cross-section of trench dug across the Trasacco fault branch at site 9. Tephra 1 and 2 are volcanic levels related to an eruption of Mt. Etna (Sicily) (from Galadini and Galli [1999]).

Simplified log of a trench excavated across the Trasacco fault in the Fucino Plain. Late Pleistocene deposits are displaced by about 1.5 m, yielding a rate of vertical separation of 0.01 mm/yr (from Galadini & Galli [1996]).

pictures.t: Distribution of offset along major Fucino faults
pictures.c: Map of proposed vertical offset distribution along the different fault branches of the Fucino seismogenic source. The maximum offset shown by the SBGF and MHF suggests that they represent the primary  fault system (from Galadini and Galli [1999]).

pictures.t: Surface traces of active or potentially active faults in central Italy
pictures.c: A number of surface active or potentially active faults identified and mapped by Bosi (1975) in a large region stretching from the Apennines piedmont east of Rome to the Adriatic coast  (Vannoli et al., [2012])

pictures.t: Surface normal faults and their slip directions in central Italy
pictures.c: Surface active normal faults offsetting the base Holocene and striking parallel to the thrust belt of the central Apennines, with their fault-slip directions (panel b), and the Quaternary basins in the hanging walls (panel c; Roberts and Michetti, [2004])
